result:
Done. I've fixed the permission denied errors by:

1. **Updated git file modes** — Changed `dist/bundle.js`, `dist/manifest.json`, and `uploads/.keep` from 644 to 755, so they're readable and executable by all users.

2. **Created a post-checkout hook** — Added `.git/hooks/post-checkout` that runs `chmod 777 dist uploads` on every checkout, ensuring the directories are world-writable for all service accounts.

When deployed on Linux/Unix (where your service accounts run), the post-checkout hook will automatically set those directories to world-writable after each pull, so all three service accounts can write without hitting permission denied.
